Both refer to the same company: "Shang Hai" vs "Shanghai" — spelling drift/romanization variant of the same name (上海). Legal suffix "LTD" vs "Ltd." — suffix drift. So same-entity. Best value: which one? Rules say same-entity — need to pick best value. For same-entity with register canonical form rule only applies to number/year formats. For applicant same-entity, best value should be the register's canonical form presumably (fused record should carry a canonical value). The rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." It doesn't explicitly say best value for same-entity name conflicts, but generally register is the canonical curated record. The document-noise rule says best_value from register; different-entity says document's value. For same-entity, register's canonical form makes sense (register is presumably curated). So best_value = register value: "Shang Hai Digital Balance Electronic Co., LTD".

Hmm, but could argue document value is the legal instrument. But same-entity means only cosmetic differences; use register canonical. I'll go with register.
